title: Groundwater availability, geochemistry, and flow pathways to public-supply wells in the Atlantic Coastal Plain and bedrock aquifers, Aiken County and part of Lexington County, South Carolina, 2015–2019
citation: Campbell, B.G., and Landmeyer, J.E., 2023, Groundwater availability, geochemistry, and flow pathways to public-supply wells in the Atlantic Coastal Plain and bedrock aquifers, Aiken County and part of Lexington County, South Carolina, 2015–2019: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report SIR-2022-5036, map scale 1:800,000.
notes: Simulated and calibrated model values (MODFLOW hydraulic conductivities, storage, water budgets, flow pathways, future scenarios) are model output and were not recorded. Abstract and overview ranges of field measurements, radium, VOCs and ages (pages 17-20) summarize per-well tables in later packets and were not recorded here. Population, climate, land use and precipitation not recorded. Figure 8 (page 30) is a schematic section, not drawn to scale, of the Aiken-Barnwell area with hydrostratigraphic names (Steed Pond, Floridan-Midville, Dublin-Midville, Meyers Branch, Allendale, Gramling, Appleton); only well labels were recorded. SUBSURFACE: base of ACP sediments about 700 ft NAVD 88 at the Fall Line to about -700 ft NAVD 88 southeastward (page 26); the bedrock modeling limit is the approximate 1,000-ft thickness of crystalline bedrock (page 22).
